decisions.executionNote: Begin left tube approach with elbow-up lift and gradual wrist pitch; live tube lies nearer than the reference.
Advance above left tube and orient fingers downward, aligned with the tube axis; keep right arm parked.
Finish downward alignment and descend slowly to the left tube body; inspect before closing.
Correct wrist yaw and lateral centering from the close-up, then close around the first tube.
Lift the closed left gripper clear of the table to check retention before reorienting toward the rack.
Tube remains between the fingers. Carry toward a left rack slot while rotating its axis upright, maintaining the elbow-up branch.
Finish bringing the retained tube upright above the left side of the rack, then inspect slot alignment before descent.
Lower the upright first tube toward the left rack opening, stopping short for a close alignment check.
Insert the first tube vertically into the left opening with a slow final descent, keeping the grip closed until depth is reached.
Release the first tube at insertion depth and withdraw backward/upward without disturbing the rack.
First tube is standing in its slot after release. Return the left arm while lifting and orienting the right arm toward the outer right tube.
Advance above the outer right tube while pitching down; continue the left arm's gradual return with joint continuity.
Align the right fingers with the outer tube's diagonal axis and descend to grasp height; finish parking the left arm.
Fine-align the outer right tube's axis from the wrist view and close the gripper around its body.
Lift the second tube away from the tabletop with the right gripper closed, checking retention before transport.
Carry the retained second tube inward within the right workspace and begin rotating it upright, using small continuous wrist increments.
Continue the second tube's smooth inward transport and upright rotation above the table, keeping clear of the seated left tube.
Finish orienting the second tube vertically above the rightmost front rack opening before insertion.
Lower the upright second tube toward the right opening with a small inward visual alignment correction; inspect before the final insertion.
Complete the second tube's slow vertical insertion into the right rack slot, keeping its orientation and grip fixed.
The second tube appears to have met the rack rim rather than seated fully. Lift slightly and shift outward toward the visible hole before retrying.
Retry the second insertion at the corrected lateral position, watching whether the tip enters the opening rather than sliding upward in the grip.
Open above the corrected slot to allow the partially seated second tube to settle, then withdraw gently and inspect its upright retention.
The second tube tipped on release, so do not count it as inserted. Clear the open fingers and inspect its resting pose for recovery.
Approach the tilted second tube again from the right with open fingers, aiming below the cap for a controlled recovery grasp.
Center the right fingers just below the tilted cap and close gently for recovery, avoiding further descent into the rack.
Lift the recovered tube clear of the rack with a closed grasp; inspect the retained axis before straightening and reinserting.
Counter the recovered tube's forward lean while raising the wrist to preserve clearance, and bring it back over the right slot.
Bring the recovered tube tip toward the visible right opening with a small outward correction and slow descent; inspect before seating.
The recovered tip now appears centered over the opening. Continue a short, slow vertical seating motion without releasing yet.
The tip still appears supported by the plate. Unload it and shift slightly back/inward toward the large hole, away from the small front-edge hole.
Lower over the newly visible large opening, maintaining the recovered tube's alignment and checking for seating rather than rim contact.
Tube is still on the far rim. Lift to unload and move toward the near-side large hole seen below the tip, reversing the prior depth correction.
Descend at the revised near-side alignment, monitoring the visible opening beneath the second tube.
The tip appears partly within the large opening. Release gradually to let it settle, then back the fingers away without dragging the tube.
The second tube is now upright after release. Withdraw and raise the right arm clear of the rack to approach the remaining tabletop tube.
Rotate the right gripper toward a top-down grasp aligned with the remaining tube's leftward diagonal, staying above the tabletop.
Finish the downward approach above the remaining tube, refining the diagonal yaw from its visible cap and tip.
Fine-center the last tube in the right wrist view and descend to body grasp height with a small yaw correction.
Move the grasp slightly toward the cap and center the body, then close around the last tube before lifting.
Lift the final tube clear while holding it closed, then verify retention before transporting to the middle slot.
The last tube is retained. Begin its upright rotation and transport toward the middle opening, staying clear of the two seated tubes.
Continue rotating the final tube upright while moving over the middle slot; maintain the closed grasp and elbow-up continuity.
Finish upright alignment above the middle opening with small continuous rotations, then inspect the tip-to-slot geometry.
Lower the upright final tube toward the middle opening, stopping above full depth to inspect alignment.
Unexpected resistance occurs above insertion depth, possibly from a neighboring tube. Lift clear and begin a straighter middle-slot approach rather than pushing down.
Reorient to a nearly straight-front middle-slot approach while keeping the tube above the rack and the right wrist in its own workspace.
Descend on the straight middle-slot approach, keeping the last tube upright and checking clearance from its neighbors.
Continue the final tube's slow vertical insertion on the clear, straight approach; keep the grasp closed until seating is checked.
Finish the shallow seating motion, release the middle tube gradually, and withdraw a little to inspect whether all three remain upright.
